events.reason: The contributor filed this under family-generative-falsification and declared it extends outcome-m4-template-doodler-pilot, but the registered scope of that family in context is specifically the Cardan table-and-grille (M5a/M5b) mechanism at high-water tier 5. Per CREDIT_IS_NOT_LINEAGE_V1 and FAMILY_IDENTITY_GUARD_V1, a declared predecessor/extends relationship and shared manuscript question do not establish same_outcome; the actual delivered capability here (Stolfi word-grammar template generator plus new real-language positive controls) is a materially different mechanism and evidence type from the grille device, so it is assessed as a new, distinct family rather than added to the occupied family's ladder. Assessed at tier 5 (informative controlled pilot / usable evidenced capability): a working, inspectable generator implementing a cited published grammar with measured 86% type coverage, plus genuinely new positive-control evidence that changes interpretation of prior results. Not tier 10: single seed, coarse 12-point grid, English-only (era-mismatched) controls, no independent execution receipt, and several core diagnostics (H2|1, final-char entropy, Zipf slope, entry-unique share) remain unmatched, so it falls short of a full discriminating/falsifying result with baselines and independent inspection at the tier-10 anchor.

families_added.scope: A distinct generative-mechanism falsification pilot implementing Stolfi's published 2000 word grammar (core/mantle/crust unimodal-hill slot structure) as a template generator embedded in an entry/topic-carryover engine, and measuring two real-language positive controls (Culpeper's Complete Herbal 1653, Alice in Wonderland) with the identical metric suite against the pinned ZL3b corpus across 12 grid variants, showing (a) real language differs from the manuscript on conditional entropy, final-char entropy and entry-private vocabulary share, reframing prior 'unmatched by content-free generators' results away from a linguistic-content reading, and (b) the published grammar covers 86% of corpus word types with zero fitting and jointly reproduces vocabulary size, ttr, word length and page-sharing, leaving a residual mechanical-repetition signature (H2|1, final-char entropy, Zipf slope, entry-unique overshoot).
families_added.acceptance_test: Run `python m4_doodler.py --corpus ../../data/corpora/ZL3b-n.txt --alice ../../data/corpora/pg11.txt --culpeper ../../data/corpora/pg49513.txt --out results/ --seed 408`; confirm results.json matches the recorded output showing control H2|1 >= 3.1 bits for both Culpeper and Alice vs 2.26 for the corpus, Stolfi grammar coverage >= 0.85 of corpus word types, and the best M4 grid variant within +/-10% of corpus types/ttr while H2|1 remains >= 0.4 bits above the corpus.
